qualifications: GPU/CPU windows are independent final stable30s tails; SurfaceFlinger capture is its own30s window. No absolute timestamp alignment between them is claimed.
GPU timestamps sample every32frames and may include command starvation/waits on the GPU timeline; they are not a pure shader-busy or utilization measurement.
CPU stage values are wall elapsed scopes; active render thread CPU covers only the render window, excluding game/AI/physics outside it.
Inclusive stages overlap: do not add details to main/sun/local or bloom/luminance to combine.
Both runs report thermalstatus0 but ON starts and ends warmer; GPU devfreq snapshots differ. No equal-clock/equal-thermal or sustained frequency comparison is established.
The first A/B pair shows a presentation and submission-cost difference with matching camera/config. It does not alone prove visual identity, long-run thermal efficiency or an all-backend gain.
Only incomplete final JSON line is dropped if present; no complete performance record is discarded as an outlier. Camera/loading transients are excluded by explicit contiguous-tail rule.

Extra grass outside local shadow frusta is commonly clipped before fragment work; removal saves draw/vertex/uniform preparation and can relieve driver waits. Do not label removed local-light elapsed time as pure fragment overdraw.
Native ON1/ON2 provide a repeated presentation/submission result; a single ANGLE ON run does not establish a definitive backend ranking.
Device timestamps are exposed through different implementations/counter widths (Native40bit, ANGLE48bit); compare sampled elapsed stage intervals cautiously.
No power, energy-per-frame or thermal reduction is derived from these runs. Higher FPS changes work per second.
